Funded postdoctoral posts, and what each one needs.

Informal enquiries are very welcome before the formal advertisement appears. A short email describing your background and what you would want to work on is enough to start a conversation. jiabao.xu@glasgow.ac.uk.
PEENOpens September 2026

Postdoctoral Research Associate in chemistry for super-resolution metabolic imaging

PEEN turns an expanded hydrogel into an active plasmonic nanoreactor, so that a standard benchtop Raman spectrometer can resolve metabolic activity at roughly 25 nm. The post is a chemistry post: the resolution comes from the sample chemistry rather than from the optics.

Essential
  • A PhD in chemistry, materials chemistry or a closely related discipline
  • Hands-on synthesis of metal nanoparticles, and experience controlling nucleation and growth in a confined or templated medium
  • Hydrogel or polymer chemistry, in particular swellable polyelectrolyte networks and covalent anchoring chemistry
  • Vibrational spectroscopy, and ideally surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) with an understanding of where enhancement comes from
Desirable
  • Expansion microscopy, or other protocols for retaining biomolecules through a physical expansion step
  • Working with microbial samples, or a willingness to learn basic microbiology alongside chemists and microbiologists
  • Python, and an interest in working with a physics-informed deep learning collaborator on reconstruction
DECODE-FATIGUEOpens September 2026

Postdoctoral Research Associate in immunology and cell biology of fatigue

DECODE-FATIGUE follows an unexpected finding: in psoriatic arthritis the extreme fatigue phenotype is biologically non-inflammatory, and carries an oxidative stress signature strongest in CD8+ T cells. The post takes that signature apart and looks for something druggable in it, so it is an immunology and cell biology post rather than a spectroscopy one.

Essential
  • A PhD in immunology, cell biology or a closely related discipline
  • PBMC isolation and handling from clinical blood samples, to a standard that holds across a multi-site cohort
  • Flow cytometry and fluorescence-activated cell sorting, including sorting T cell subsets to purity
  • Cell-based functional assays, in particular readouts of oxidative stress and mitochondrial function
Desirable
  • T cell biology, and CD8+ T cell biology in particular
  • In vitro pharmacological modulation experiments aimed at target validation
  • Working with clinical cohorts and the governance that comes with them
  • An interest in learning single-cell Raman spectroscopy; no prior spectroscopy experience is expected
